A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MACPO study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including relocated material and v2's additional experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original helpfulness and harmlessness experiments, reward-model scores, GPT-4 and human evaluations, teacher-count analyses, and component ablations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments on iterative baselines, perplexity filtering, MT-Bench, and teacher/student response quality in Appendix G.

M1.justification: MACPO retains the same mutual learning procedure, lowest-perplexity positive-label selection, fixed negative agents, and combined DPO/SFT objective. The W/S notation and initialization/optimization labels clarify the existing procedure; student-first updating already appears in v1's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 adds MT-Bench evaluation covering writing, roleplay, reasoning, mathematics, coding, extraction, STEM, and humanities. This substantially broadens the explicitly evaluated task coverage beyond the retained HH-Helpful, HH-Harmless, and PKU-SafeRLHF experiments.

E2.justification: The six main baselines remain unchanged. Appendix G.1 and Table 4 additionally evaluate iterative adaptations of RLAIF and RLCD that regenerate samples each round, whereas v1 reports only their single-round versions. MT-Bench reuses the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 introduces three-round resampling comparisons for RLAIF/RLCD, GPT-4 scoring from 1 to 10 on MT-Bench without additional fine-tuning, and a diagnostic using 100 sampled examples. Existing splits, backbones, training epochs, and main evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Newly explained reward scaling documents the existing evaluation.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds controls testing iterative RLAIF/RLCD performance, an ablation replacing perplexity filtering with random label selection under three teachers, and an analysis relating student perplexity to teacher/student response rewards. These substantially extend the investigation of central design choices beyond the retained ablations, teacher analyses, and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the p < 0.05 sign tests in Tables 2–3 and the two position-swapped GPT-4 evaluations. V2 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-training-run reporting, confidence intervals, or error bars; its new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original figure results are unchanged, but Tables 4–7 add substantial new outcomes. Third-round RLAIF/RLCD average rewards are 53.34/55.28; removing filtering gives 64.50 versus MACPO's 67.85; MT-Bench scores are 4.63 for MACPO and 4.59 for RLCD. Teacher-label perplexity/reward measurements and generation-time estimates are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10) retain their mathematical content apart from model notation. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v2 introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, or derivations. Its terminology clarifications and empirical reward-processing explanation do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: MACPO's two strategies improve both strong students and weak teachers, and additional teachers support better iterative alignment. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds a rationale for updating the student first, interprets the new filtering and label-quality analyses, argues for transfer to general alignment tasks, and discusses generation efficiency. Existing limitations are retained in Appendix H, with additional future application areas listed.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly documents concatenating conversation history with the answer and applying sigmoid scaling followed by multiplication by 100. Appendix E.2 reports approximate generation times of five minutes for 7B models and two hours for 70B models. The code/data access link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: V2 adds Marion, Muennighoff, and Wenzek citations supporting perplexity filtering, plus references for future applications. The weak-to-strong discussion replaces the ConTrans citation with Yang et al.'s Super(ficial)-alignment work. The main positioning relative to alignment and multi-agent research remains stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. Changes include explicit familiar/unfamiliar terminology, simplified model notation, author-year citations, additional appendix subsections, and relocation of Limitations to Appendix H. These are targeted clarifications and organizational changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds four appendix tables and adopts ICLR title, header, and heading formatting. Existing figures retain their graphics and data, while layout reflow relocates Table 3, Figure 3, and several appendix figures. The original table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: V1 already provided automatic and human evaluations and several component ablations. V2 strengthens that evidence with iterative baseline controls and a direct filtering ablation, while clarifying reward computation and runtime. MT-Bench adds useful breadth, although the 4.63 versus 4.59 lead over RLCD has no reported uncertainty. The gains are meaningful but mainly strengthen and clarify the existing empirical case.
